description: Michael's deterministic task prioritization: the published components, their default weights and the constants they use. Read by services/intelligence/app/tasks/prioritization.py (which computes) and src/lib/task-priority-format.ts (which explains). A score is 100 × the weighted mean of the components that apply to a task; a component that cannot apply (no dependencies in LifestyleOS, no estimate, unknown history) is left out and the remaining weights renormalized, never guessed.

components.name: user_priority
components.label: Your priority
components.description: The priority you set: low 0.1, medium 0.4, high 0.75, urgent 1.

components.name: due_proximity
components.label: Due date
components.description: 1 when overdue or due today, halving every 7 days after that; 0 with no due date.

components.name: goal_alignment
components.label: Goal or project
components.description: Personal: 0.6 for supporting an active goal, rising to 1 as its target date nears. Work: the project's priority (low 0.3, medium 0.6, high 0.9), weighted up as its target date nears. 0 when unlinked.

components.name: blocking_impact
components.label: Holds up other work
components.description: Work only: 0.5 for one open task waiting on this one, 0.75 for two, approaching 1.

components.name: effort_vs_time_left
components.label: Effort vs time left
components.description: Remaining (or estimated) minutes against 240 focus minutes per day until the due date, capped at 1. Applies only with both an estimate and a due date.

components.name: postponement_history
components.label: Postponed before
components.description: 0.5 after one postponement, 0.75 after two, approaching 1. Applies only where due-date history is recorded.

ordering: Actionable tasks first (not BLOCKED and no open blocker), then score descending, then due date ascending with undated last, then priority descending, then the order the server sent.
